sections.heading: Industry's role — and the policy evolution to 1991

blocks.text: Industry (~**28-30% of GVA**; manufacturing ~17%) is development's **productivity escalator**: it absorbs farm labour at higher wages, generates innovation-linkage density (one manufacturing job ~2-3 indirect), earns tradables, and builds strategic capacity (defence-energy-pharma). India's policy evolution is a **five-act play**: (1) **IPR 1948** — mixed economy declared; (2) **IPR 1956** — the 'economic constitution': Schedule A (17 state-monopoly industries), B (state-led), C (private); the Mahalanobis heavy-industry alignment; (3) **the licence-permit raj's consolidation** — Industries Act 1951's licensing, MRTP 1969 (size policing), FERA 1973 (foreign-equity caps ~40%; IBM-Coca-Cola exits 1977), small-scale reservation (~800+ items); (4) **1980s creep-liberalisation** — 1980 IPR's pragmatism, broad-banding, MODVAT (1986), seeds of exit; (5) **1991** — the rupture (IDI-039).

rows: Capability
Heavy-industrial base (steel-machines-power), scientific establishment, entrepreneurial survival
Diversified but inefficient — world-frontier gaps widened
Control regime
Direction of scarce capital to plan priorities
**Licensing = queueing + rent-seeking; MRTP punished scale; FERA repelled technology**
Protection
Infant-industry space
Infants never graduated — tariff walls bred high-cost habits; export pessimism self-fulfilled (~0.5% world-trade share by 1990)
Public-sector primacy
Temples built (IDI-040's file)
Soft budgets, administered prices, chronic under-returns

items: **The design-vs-drift distinction**: 1956's logic (scarce capital, defence needs, equity aims) was coherent FOR ITS TIME; the failure was **non-adaptation** — controls built for scarcity persisting into rigidity: critique the drift, credit the design.

**The 1980s bridge**: growth rose to ~5.5% on creeping deregulation + fiscal expansion — proving controls were binding, while the borrowed-boom's BoP bill set up 1991: the decade as both proof and prelude.

**AP thread**: the pre-91 public-sector map placed **Visakhapatnam's shipyard (1941/nationalised 1961), HAL-adjacent units, BHEL(R&D)-Hyderabad-era**, and the port-steel dream (Vizag Steel's 1970s agitation — 'Visakha ukku, Andhrula hakku' — plant commissioned 1990-92): the state's industrial baseline was plan-era public investment.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — industrial-policy evolution to 1991

items: **The policy arc:** **IPR 1948** (mixed economy) → **IPR 1956** (the 'economic constitution', Mahalanobis heavy-industry model, three schedules) → 1970s licence-permit raj (**MRTP 1969, FERA 1973**) → partial liberalisation of the 1980s.

**The Mahalanobis/Nehruvian model:** state-led, heavy-industry-first, import-substituting industrialisation (ISI) with a dominant public sector — built a capital-goods base but created inefficiency, shortages and a low '**Hindu rate of growth**' (~3.5%).
**Why it stalled:** licensing bred rent-seeking and delays; small-scale reservations and protectionism blunted competitiveness; the 1991 BoP crisis forced the pivot.
**Assessment:** the ISI era built industrial foundations and self-reliance but at the cost of efficiency and consumer welfare — the classic 'infant industry that never grew up' critique.

prelimsPointers: **IPR 1956** — the basis of state-led industrialisation; classified industries into three schedules.
'**Hindu rate of growth**' (~3.5%) — term coined by Raj Krishna for India's slow pre-reform growth.
**MRTP Act 1969** (monopolies) and **FERA 1973** (foreign exchange) epitomised the control regime.
**IPR 1956** — 'economic constitution': **Schedule A (17 exclusive-state), B (12 progressive-state), C (private)**.
**Industries (D&R) Act 1951** — the licensing statute; **MRTP 1969** (assets-threshold scrutiny) → replaced by **Competition Act 2002**.
**FERA 1973** capped foreign equity (~40%) — IBM & Coca-Cola exits (1977); replaced by **FEMA 1999**.
**MODVAT (1986)** — input-credit excise: GST's conceptual ancestor.
Small-scale reservation peaked ~**800+ items**; dismantled through the 2000s (ended 2015).
India's world-merchandise-export share fell to ~**0.5% (1990)** from ~2% (1950).
**Visakhapatnam Steel Plant** — sanctioned after the 1966 'Visakha ukku' agitation (32 lives); commissioned 1990-92; RINL's privatisation-revival debates current.

The 1980s proved the controls binding and the financing unsustainable — assess the bridge decade.
Write AP's plan-era industrial baseline — shipyard to steel movement — as the regional face of national policy.

The plan-era belief that world markets couldn't absorb Indian exports — protection's self-fulfilling premise.
Temporary protection for learning industries — valid in design, corrupted by permanence.

sections.heading: 1991 — the New Industrial Policy and its impact

blocks.text: The **July 24, 1991 Statement on Industrial Policy** — born of the BoP crisis (reserves ~2 weeks' imports; gold pledged; IMF programme) — dismantled four walls in one stroke: **(1) De-licensing** — industrial licensing abolished except a security-environment shortlist (now ~4-5 sectors); **(2) Public-sector pruning** — reservation cut from 17 to 8 (now ~2-3: atomic energy, rail operations' core), sick-PSU review to BIFR, disinvestment begun; **(3) MRTP defanged** — pre-entry size scrutiny abolished (competition policy re-founded 2002); **(4) Foreign walls lowered** — FDI to 51% automatic in 34 industries (then ever-upward), FERA→FEMA, technology-agreement freedom. Companion reforms: trade (tariffs ~150%→~10% average by 2007), exchange rate (devaluation→managed float), finance (SEBI, private banks).

rows: Growth & efficiency
GDP trend up (~6-7% post-91 vs ~4-5%); TFP gains in de-licensed industries; corporate deepening (the Infosys-to-Bharti class)
Manufacturing SHARE stagnated (~16-17%) — reform freed industry without igniting industrialisation: the central puzzle
Competition & consumers
Choice-quality revolutions (autos-telecom-aviation); prices of tradables disciplined
Import competition + China shock (2001-) hit labour-intensive segments (toys-electronics's hollowing)
Employment
Services absorbed the educated; organised-manufacturing jobs grew slowly
**Jobless-industrialisation critique**; informality persisted ~90%
Regions & firms
Agglomeration winners (west-south corridors — TN-Gujarat-Maharashtra-Karnataka; **AP's post-91 rise via Hyderabad-then-coast**)
Laggard-state divergence; the missing-middle firm distribution survived reform

items: **The mature verdict**: 1991 removed the state's VETO but not industry's BINDING CONSTRAINTS (land-labour-logistics-credit-skills) — hence liberation without transformation; the post-2014 stack (GST, IBC, PLI, Gati Shakti, codes) is best read as **1991's unfinished second half**.

**AP's 1991 story**: liberalisation + a reformist-state posture made undivided AP an early adopter (power reforms, IT-Hyderabad, the first EoDB-style single windows) — residual AP inherited the posture and re-aimed it at the coast (IDA-043).
**Craft**: four-walls dismantled + companion reforms + the two-column impact ledger + the unfinished-second-half thesis.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — 1991 reforms (LPG) & their impact

items: **The trigger:** the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis (reserves down to ~2 weeks of imports; gold pledged) forced structural adjustment under Narasimha Rao/Manmohan Singh.

**LPG measures:** **Liberalisation** (abolished industrial licensing for most sectors, de-reserved), **Privatisation** (disinvestment begins, PSU reform), **Globalisation** (rupee devaluation & convertibility, lower tariffs, FDI opening, **MRTP diluted, FERA→FEMA 1999**).
**Impact — the credit side:** growth accelerated (services boom, IT, telecom revolution), poverty fell, a large middle class emerged, forex reserves swelled, and global integration deepened.

**Impact — the debit side:** jobless growth, rising inequality, agrarian neglect, and vulnerability to global shocks — the reforms addressed the product market more than land, labour and factor markets ('reform of 1991 vs the unfinished reforms').

prelimsPointers: **1991 reforms** under PM Narasimha Rao and FM Manmohan Singh (LPG: Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation).
**FEMA 1999** replaced FERA 1973; **New Industrial Policy 1991** abolished licensing for most industries.
mainsAngles: 'The 1991 reforms transformed India but left the factor markets untouched' — evaluate.

Peak tariffs ~**150% (1991) → ~10% average (2007-08)**; rupee devalued ~18-19% (July 1991, two steps).
Reserves at crisis trough ≈ **$1.1-1.2 bn (~2 weeks' imports)**; **47 tonnes gold pledged** (Bank of England/UBS).
Manufacturing's GVA share has stayed ~**16-17%** through three post-reform decades — the stagnation fact.

sections.heading: The public sector — contribution and reckoning

rows: **Contribution**

Built the base no private balance-sheet could (steel-power-machines-oil), infrastructure & backward-region industrialisation (**Vizag Steel's coastal-AP anchor role**), employment-training academies (the PSU-trained manager class), strategic autonomy (ISRO-DRDO-BHEL-HAL's ecosystems), market-failure services (rail-post-rural banking after 1969 nationalisation)
**The reckoning**

Under-returns on ~₹17-lakh-crore+ invested capital (CPSE survey era), soft-budget losses (BSNL-Air-India's fiscal drains pre-exit), administered-price distortions, over-manning, board politicisation — 'temples' becoming 'trusts of last resort'
**LPG's impact on PSUs**

Competition ended monopolies (telecom's lesson: BSNL vs private), MoU-Ratna autonomy ladders (**Maharatna-11, Navratna-26, Miniratna-scale**), listing's discipline (LIC 2022 the giant), and the sorting — profitable strategics (NTPC-PowerGrid-ONGC) vs chronic patients
**Disinvestment & privatisation arc**

Minority sales (1991-98) → **strategic sales (1999-2004: BALCO, Hindustan Zinc, VSNL, IPCL)** → the ETF-listing decade (receipts without control transfer) → **the 2021 turn: Air India's Tata sale + the New PSE Policy (strategic sectors' bare-minimum presence; non-strategic exit)** — with **NINL (2022)** done, RINL-Vizag's on-off saga (2024-25 revival package instead of sale — the AP-political economy exhibit), IDBI's sale in motion

items: **Privatisation's case**: allocative efficiency, fiscal release (subsidy-to-capex), Air India's turnaround signs, Hindustan-Zinc-BALCO's post-sale growth; **the counter-case**: strategic-sector prudence, monopoly-transfer risk (sell into competition, not into monopoly), employment-region shocks (the Vizag-plant emotion — 'Visakha ukku' round two), family-silver timing critiques.

**The synthesis policy**: the **2021 PSE policy's** four strategic sectors (atomic-space-defence; transport-telecom; power-petroleum-minerals; banking-insurance-financial) with 'bare minimum' presence + non-strategic privatisation-closure — ownership as portfolio choice, not theology; execution (beyond Air India-NINL) remains the test.

**AP register**: RINL (the state's industrial totem — package-revival 2025 over privatisation), HSL shipyard, NTPC-Simhadri, the port-PSU interface — public capital's coastal footprint and its political economy.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — the public sector, contribution & reckoning

items: **Rationale (Nehruvian):** build heavy industry, occupy 'commanding heights', ensure balanced regional growth, curb concentration of wealth, and generate surplus for reinvestment.
**Contribution:** created the capital-goods, steel, energy and defence base; Maharatnas/Navratnas (ONGC, NTPC, IOC, SAIL, BHEL) remain strategic; employment and public purpose.

**Mature debate:** the state should exit commercial activity where markets work, retain strategic/public-good sectors, and use PSU capital efficiently — 'government has no business to be in business' vs the case for strategic public capacity.

sections.heading: Core industries — and the MSME universe

blocks.text: The **eight core industries** (ICI, ~40% weight in IIP): **coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement, electricity** — infrastructure's input spine, each with its problem file: coal's logistics-quality, crude-gas's declining domestic output (import ~88%/50%), fertiliser's subsidy-urea distortion (~₹1.7-2 lakh cr subsidy), steel-cement's demand-cyclicality + carbon exposure (CBAM's shadow), electricity's DISCOM chain. **MSMEs** are the other pole: **~6+ crore units, ~11-12 crore jobs, ~30% of GDP, ~45% of exports** — classified (2020, composite): micro ≤₹1 cr investment & ≤₹5 cr turnover; small ≤10/50; medium ≤50/250 (2025 budget raised bands ~2.5x — investment ≤2.5/25/125 cr, turnover ≤10/100/500 cr).

rows: Credit
~₹25-30 lakh cr gap; collateral-information barriers
**Mudra (~₹27 lakh cr cumulative), CGTMSE guarantees (limit ₹10 cr era), 59-minute loans, TReDS receivables, PSL sub-targets**
**Sickness & stress**
Definition — SMA-NPA slide; causes: delayed payments (the #1 killer — buyers' float on MSME working capital), demand shocks, tech obsolescence

**Samadhaan portal (delayed-payment MSEFC councils), 45-day payment rule (Sec 43B(h) IT Act — the 2024 enforcement lever)**, revival framework (RBI's restructuring windows; pre-pack insolvency for MSMEs 2021), ECLGS's ₹3.7-lakh-cr COVID guarantee
Formalisation & market
Registration gaps, procurement access
**Udyam (~5+ crore registrations), GeM's 25% MSE procurement mandate**, PMEGP, cluster development (SFURTI-MSE-CDP), **RAMP (World Bank $500 mn)**, ZED certification
Technology & scale
The missing-middle graduation fear (losing benefits on growing)
Graduated-benefit continuation (3-yr protection on upgradation), CHAMPIONS handholding

items: **Core industries' common thread**: each is a **regulated-price network industry** where government IS the market-maker — their problems are policy problems (fertiliser's NBS-urea gap, coal's rail rakes, DISCOM dues) more than firm problems: the analytical key.

**MSME's deepest fix is payment discipline + data-credit**: the 45-day rule (43B(h)) attacks the float; Udyam-GST-AA data builds lendability — cash-flow lending replacing collateral lending is the structural answer.

**AP register**: core — Vizag refinery-steel-fertiliser (Coromandel), Krishnapatnam power; MSME — ~26 lakh registered units era, aqua-feed & food-processing clusters, Nellore-Prakasam's granite-subabul micro-economies, the constituency-MSME-park policy (IDA-043) — the state as both poles' host.

sections.heading: The manufacturing push — the policy stack since 2011

rows: **National Manufacturing Policy 2011**
25% GDP share + 100 mn jobs by 2022; **NIMZs** (giant self-governed zones with exit-flexibility)
Targets missed wholesale; NIMZs largely paper (land-scale unrealism) — cite as the lesson in announcement-vs-plumbing
**Make in India (2014)**
25 sectors, EoDB climb ((142→63 World Bank), FDI liberalisation, brand umbrella
FDI & ease delivered; share-of-GDP didn't move — branding met binding constraints
**SEZs (Act 2005)**
Duty-free export enclaves; ~270+ operational

Exports concentrated (IT-pharma-petro); MAT-sunset blows (2011/2020) stalled the model; **DESH Bill** (development hubs, DTA flexibility) the pending redesign; AP's port-linked SEZs the better performers (IDA-044)
**Corridors & parks**
11-corridor NICDC programme; plug-and-play (the AP chapter IDA-044); **PM MITRA textile parks (7), medical-devices & bulk-drug parks (AP's Kakinada-era bids)**
Infrastructure-first logic sound; occupancy the test
**Startup India (2016)**
DPIIT recognition (**~1.5-1.6 lakh startups; 110+ unicorns**), tax holidays, Fund-of-Funds (₹10,000 cr), self-certification
The ecosystem win — world #3; concentration in services-metros the caveat
**14 sectors, ~₹1.97 lakh crore**, output-linked payouts
Electronics the star (mobile exports ~$15→29 bn); pharma-drones good; some sectors slow-disbursing — 'PLI works where scale-economics needed a nudge, not a crutch'

items: **The strategy's evolution in one line**: from **zones (SEZ)** to **brands (MII)** to **subsidies (PLI)** to **plumbing (GST-IBC-codes-Gati Shakti)** — each layer learning the last's limit; the frontier is factor markets (land-labour-logistics-skills) + the China+1 window.

**Honest metrics**: manufacturing GVA share still ~17%; but **electronics' export transformation, GCC-services-manufacturing blur, and FDI's reorientation** show segment-level wins — write 'aggregate stagnation, segment breakthroughs'.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — the manufacturing push since 2011

items: **The policy stack:** **National Manufacturing Policy 2011 (25% GDP, 100 mn jobs target)** → **Make in India (2014)** → **Atmanirbhar Bharat (2020)** → **PLI schemes (14 sectors, ~₹2 lakh crore)** for electronics, semiconductors (India Semiconductor Mission), pharma, autos, solar, etc.

**Enablers:** **PM Gati Shakti & National Logistics Policy** (cut logistics cost), labour codes, Ease of Doing Business, corporate-tax cuts (2019), and the **'China+1'** supply-chain shift (Apple/electronics assembly moving to India).

**Reality check:** manufacturing's GDP share is still ~15-17% (below the 25% target); success in electronics/mobile assembly & pharma, but deeper value-addition, R&D and component ecosystems are the next frontier.
**AP hook:** VCIC corridor, electronics/auto (Kia), pharma clusters, and port-led manufacturing are AP's stake in the national manufacturing push.

prelimsPointers: **PLI (Production Linked Incentive)** schemes cover **14 sectors**; the **India Semiconductor Mission** anchors chip manufacturing.
**National Manufacturing Policy 2011** targeted 25% of GDP and 100 million manufacturing jobs.
mainsAngles: 'Despite Make in India and PLI, manufacturing's share has not risen' — diagnose the constraints and suggest the way forward.

prelimsPointers: **NMP 2011**: 25% manufacturing share + 100 mn jobs by 2022 — unmet; **NIMZs** the zone instrument.
**Make in India (25 Sept 2014)** — 25 sectors; India's EoDB rank **142 (2014) → 63 (2019)**.
**SEZ Act 2005**; ~270+ operational SEZs; **DESH Bill** the proposed successor framework.
**Startup India (16 Jan 2016)**: DPIIT-recognised ~**1.5-1.6 lakh startups; 110+ unicorns**; Fund-of-Funds ₹10,000 crore (SIDBI).
**PLI: 14 sectors, ₹1.97 lakh crore (2020-21)**; mobile exports ~$29 bn era — electronics the flagship.
**PM MITRA**: 7 mega textile parks (2023 sites); bulk-drug & medical-device parks scheme rounds.
**Semicon India (₹76,000 cr)** — fabs-ATMP incentives (Micron's Sanand ATMP the first big landing).
mainsAngles: Zones, brands, subsidies, plumbing — periodise the manufacturing push and what each layer learnt.
PLI works as nudge, fails as crutch — evaluate sector-wise with electronics as proof of concept.
SEZs enclaved success and stalled — assess the model and the DESH redesign's promises.
Aggregate flat, segments breaking through — reconcile manufacturing's share stagnation with its export transformations.
Startup India built the world's third ecosystem — audit its depth, concentration and industrial linkage.

glossary.definition: National Investment & Manufacturing Zone — the 2011 policy's giant self-governed industrial townships, largely unrealised.
Output-conditional subsidies for scale manufacturing — paying for production, not promises.
A private startup valued above $1 billion — the ecosystem-depth marker.
Global buyers' supply-chain diversification beyond China — India's manufacturing window.
The proposed Development of Enterprise and Services Hubs law — SEZ 2.0 with domestic-market flexibility.
Global Capability Centres — MNC tech-operations hubs; the services-manufacturing blur India dominates.
